questions.q: A strip of cloth is 5 3/10 m long. Written in tenths only, its length is
questions.a: 53/10 m, because 5 units are 50 tenths and 50 + 3 = 53 tenths.

questions.q: Match each length in Column I with the same length in Column II. Column I: 1. 2 6/10, 2. 26/100, 3. 2 6/100, 4. 206/10. Column II: A. 206/100, B. 26 tenths, C. 26 hundredths, D. 20 6/10.
An eraser is 3 7/10 cm long. (a) Write its length in tenths only. (b) How many more tenths of a centimetre are needed to make it 4 cm long?
questions.a: (a) 3 units = 30 tenths, so 3 7/10 cm = 37/10 cm. (b) 4 cm = 40 tenths, and 40 - 37 = 3, so 3 more tenths (3/10 cm) are needed.
s: Part (b): uses 4 cm = 40 tenths and finds 3 tenths more

questions.q: A basket-maker in Assam has two cane strips of 4 6/10 8/100 m and 2 5/10 7/100 m. (a) Find their total length. (b) How much longer is the first strip than the second? (c) Write the total length in hundredths only.
questions.a: (a) 4 + 2 = 6 units, 6 + 5 = 11 tenths, 8 + 7 = 15 hundredths; 15 hundredths = 1 tenth 5 hundredths and 12 tenths = 1 unit 2 tenths, so the total is 7 2/10 5/100 m. (b) 4 6/10 8/100 - 2 5/10 7/100 = 2 1/10 1/100 m. (c) 7 2/10 5/100 m = 725/100 m.
s: Part (a): adds place by place and regroups to get 7 2/10 5/100 m
Part (c): writes the total as 725/100 m

questions.q: Assertion (A): A length of 2 15/10 m is the same as 3 5/10 m. Reason (R): 10 one-tenths make 1 unit.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: 15 tenths = 10 tenths + 5 tenths = 1 unit and 5 tenths, so 2 15/10 = 3 5/10, and that regrouping is exactly R.

questions.q: A hardware shop in Kanpur has a coil of rope 6 4/10 m long. It sells 1 7/10 m to one customer and 2 2/10 m to another. (a) Find the total length sold. (b) Find the length of rope left in the coil. (c) Write the length left in tenths only.
questions.a: (a) 1 7/10 + 2 2/10 = 3 9/10 m. (b) 6 4/10 - 3 9/10: we cannot take 9 tenths from 4 tenths, so split one unit: 5 14/10 - 3 9/10 = 2 5/10 m. (c) 2 5/10 m = 25/10 m.
s: Part (b): regroups 1 unit as 10 tenths and finds 2 5/10 m left

questions.q: In the decimal 46.27, which digit is in the hundredths place?
questions.a: 7 is in the hundredths place (2 is in the tenths place).

questions.q: A lab sheet records a powder as 32 tenths and 15 hundredths of a gram. Written as a single decimal, the mass is
questions.a: 3.35 g: 32 tenths = 3.2 and 15 hundredths = 0.15, and 3.2 + 0.15 = 3.35.

questions.q: (a) How many thousandths make one tenth? (b) How many tenths make one ten?
questions.a: (a) 100 thousandths make one tenth. (b) 100 tenths make one ten (10 tenths make 1 unit and 10 units make 1 ten).

questions.q: True or False: The decimal 9.06 is read as 'nine point six'. Give the reason or the correct reading.
questions.a: False. 9.06 means 9 ones, 0 tenths and 6 hundredths, so it is read 'nine point zero six'; 'nine point six' is 9.6.
s: Gives the reading 'nine point zero six' with the place values

questions.q: Consider these statements. Statement I: In 30.4 the digit 4 stands for 4 tenths. Statement II: In 3.04 the digit 3 stands for 3 tens. Statement III: 304 hundredths written as a decimal is 30.4. Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: Statement I only. In 3.04 the 3 stands for 3 ones, and 304 hundredths is 3.04, not 30.4.

questions.q: A shopkeeper in Erode writes his stock in an unusual way: rice 1234 tenths of a kg, dal 1234 hundredths of a kg and salt 1234 thousandths of a kg. (a) Write each quantity as a decimal in kg. (b) In each of the three decimals, what is the value of the digit 3? (c) How many times as heavy as the dal is the rice? (d) Find the total weight of the dal and the salt. (e) A helper copies the salt as 12.34 kg. By how many kg is his entry too large?
questions.a: (a) Rice 123.4 kg, dal 12.34 kg, salt 1.234 kg. (b) In 123.4 the 3 is 3 ones; in 12.34 it is 3 tenths (0.3); in 1.234 it is 3 hundredths (0.03). (c) Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so the rice is 10 times as heavy as the dal. (d) 12.34 + 1.234 = 13.574 kg. (e) 12.34 - 1.234 = 11.106 kg too large.
s: Part (b): gives the value of 3 as 3 ones, 3 tenths and 3 hundredths
Part (c): 10 times, because a tenth is 10 hundredths

questions.q: Which of these decimals is equal to 0.7?
questions.a: 0.70, because both are 7 tenths; a zero at the right end does not change the value.

questions.q: A shopkeeper writes the price of a pencil in five ways: ₹6.30, ₹6.03, ₹06.30, ₹6.300 and ₹0.63. How many of these are equal to ₹6.3?
questions.a: Three: ₹6.30, ₹06.30 and ₹6.300 are all 6 ones and 3 tenths; ₹6.03 and ₹0.63 are different.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 2.50 m and 2.5 m are the same length. Reason (R): A zero written at the right end of the decimal part does not change the place value of any other digit.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: both lengths are 2 units and 5 tenths because the extra zero leaves every digit in its place.

questions.q: True or False: 0.300 kg of sugar is heavier than 0.3 kg of sugar. Give the reason.
questions.a: False. Both 0.300 and 0.3 mean 3 tenths of a kg; the zeros at the right end do not change the value, so the weights are equal.
s: Explains both are 3 tenths, so equal

questions.q: Ravi says: 'Removing a zero from a decimal never changes its value, so 5.80 = 5.8 and 5.08 = 5.8.' (a) Check whether 5.80 = 5.8. (b) Check whether 5.08 = 5.8. (c) Find the difference between 5.8 and 5.08, and say which zeros can be dropped safely.
questions.a: (a) True: both are 5 units and 8 tenths. (b) False: in 5.08 the zero holds the tenths place, so 8 is 8 hundredths, while in 5.8 it is 8 tenths. (c) 5.8 - 5.08 = 0.72. Only zeros at the right end of the decimal part can be dropped; a zero right after the point cannot.
s: Part (b): shows 5.08 is not 5.8 (hundredths vs tenths)
Part (c): finds 0.72 and states the rule for dropping zeros

questions.q: A goldsmith's scale in Thrissur always shows three digits after the point. Four readings in grams are 3.040, 3.400, 0.340 and 3.004. (a) Write each reading in its shortest form without changing its value. (b) Which reading is the same as 3.4 g? (c) Arrange the four readings in ascending order. (d) Find the difference between the largest and the smallest reading.
s: Part (a): drops only the right-end zeros

questions.q: A balance in a Guntur lab shows masses in grams with three digits after the point: 0.050, 0.500, 0.005, 0.550 and 0.505. A trainee rewrites them 'without the extra zeros' as 0.05, 0.5, 0.5, 0.55 and 0.55. (a) Which of his five rewrites are correct? (b) For each wrong rewrite, give the correct short form. (c) By how much is each wrong rewrite larger than the real reading? (d) Arrange the five real readings in ascending order. (e) Find the total of the five real readings.
s: Part (a): picks the three correct rewrites
Part (b): 0.005 and 0.505, zeros that hold a place cannot go

questions.q: Which of these numbers is the greatest: 5.4, 5.38, 5.093, 5.399?
questions.a: 5.4: all have 5 units, and 5.4 has the most tenths (4).

questions.q: On a number line, the gap from 3 to 4 is divided into 10 equal parts. The 6th mark after 3 stands for
questions.a: 3.6, because each part is one tenth and 6 tenths after 3 is 3.6.

questions.q: On a number line the gap from 20 to 25 is divided into 10 equal parts. Which number is at the 7th mark after 20?
questions.a: 23.5: 5 units in 10 parts makes each part 0.5, and 7 parts is 3.5 more than 20.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 4.7 is greater than 4.69. Reason (R): 4.69 has more digits after the decimal point than 4.7.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A: both statements are true, but 4.7 is greater because it has 7 tenths against 6 tenths; the number of digits does not decide.

questions.q: Arrange in descending order: 7.2, 7.02, 7.22, 7.202.
questions.a: All have 7 units. 7.02 has 0 tenths, so it is the smallest. The others have 2 tenths; comparing hundredths and thousandths gives 7.22 > 7.202 > 7.2. Order: 7.22, 7.202, 7.2, 7.02.
s: Compares the next places and gives 7.22, 7.202, 7.2, 7.02

questions.q: Which number is greater in each pair? (a) 0.6 or 0.58 (b) 12.3 or 2.99 (c) 4.405 or 4.45
questions.a: (a) 0.6, since 6 tenths is more than 5 tenths. (b) 12.3, since 12 units is more than 2 units. (c) 4.45, since both have 4 tenths but 5 hundredths is more than 0 hundredths.

questions.q: A mango farmer in Ratnagiri grades his mangoes for a shop in Mumbai. A mango is 'Grade A' only if it weighs more than 0.35 kg. His daughter weighs five mangoes on a digital scale and notes: P 0.352 kg, Q 0.325 kg, R 0.4 kg, S 0.305 kg and T 0.35 kg. A gift box can hold mangoes weighing at most 0.8 kg in all. (a) Which mango is the heaviest? (b) Arrange the five weights in ascending order. (c) Which mangoes are Grade A? (d) Can both Grade A mangoes go into one gift box? Show your working.
questions.a: (a) R (0.4 kg has the most tenths). (b) 0.305 < 0.325 < 0.35 < 0.352 < 0.4 (S, Q, T, P, R). (c) P and R; T is exactly 0.35 kg, not more. (d) 0.352 + 0.4 = 0.752 kg, which is not more than 0.8 kg, so yes.
s: Part (c): P and R only, with T excluded
Part (d): 0.752 kg is within 0.8 kg, so yes

questions.q: A number line is drawn from 8 to 9 and the gap is divided into 10 equal parts. Point A is on the 2nd mark after 8 and point B is on the 7th mark. The part from 8.7 to 8.8 is then magnified and divided into 10 equal parts, and point C is on the 4th mark after 8.7. (a) Write the number at A. (b) Write the number at B. (c) Write the number at C. (d) Arrange A, B, C and 8.704 in ascending order. (e) Which of B and C is closer to 8.75? Give both gaps.
questions.a: (a) A = 8.2. (b) B = 8.7. (c) Each small part is one hundredth, so C = 8.74. (d) 8.2 < 8.7 < 8.704 < 8.74. (e) B is 0.05 from 8.75 and C is 0.01 from it, so C is closer.
s: Part (c): 8.74, each small part a hundredth

questions.q: 1 paisa written in rupees is
questions.a: ₹0.01, because 100 paise make 1 rupee, so 1 paisa is one hundredth of a rupee.

questions.q: A pencil lead is 84 mm long. In centimetres its length is
questions.a: 8.4 cm, because 1 mm = 0.1 cm, so 84 mm = 84 tenths of a cm.

questions.q: Consider these statements. Statement I: 1 m = 1000 mm. Statement II: 305 g = 0.35 kg. Statement III: 7 paise = ₹0.07. Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: Statements I and III only. 305 g is 305 thousandths of a kg, which is 0.305 kg, not 0.35 kg.

questions.q: (a) Write 3 kg 45 g in kilograms. (b) Write 2.08 m in centimetres.
True or False: 1 mm is the same as 0.001 m. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm, so 1 m = 1000 mm; therefore 1 mm = 1/1000 m = 0.001 m.
s: Uses 1 m = 1000 mm to show 1 mm = 0.001 m

questions.q: Convert each quantity. (a) 7 mm into centimetres. (b) 63 cm into metres. (c) 2340 g into kilograms. (d) 85 paise into rupees. (e) 4.5 cm into millimetres.

A school in Vijayawada tells parents that a Class 7 school bag should weigh at most 3 kg. Meena weighs the things in her bag on a kitchen scale that shows grams: maths book 475 g, science book 520 g, notebooks 1150 g, water bottle 750 g and tiffin box 380 g. (a) Write the weight of the maths book in kilograms. (b) Write the weight of the notebooks in kilograms. (c) Find the total weight of the bag in kilograms. (d) Is the bag within the 3 kg limit? If not, by how much is it over?
s: Part (d): not within the limit, over by 0.275 kg

questions.q: Sneha says: '3 kg 5 g is 3.5 kg, and 3 m 5 cm is 3.5 m.' (a) Write 3 kg 5 g correctly in kg. (b) Write 3 m 5 cm correctly in m. (c) By how many grams is Sneha's 3.5 kg heavier than the real 3 kg 5 g?
questions.a: (a) 5 g = 5/1000 kg = 0.005 kg, so 3.005 kg. (b) 5 cm = 5/100 m = 0.05 m, so 3.05 m. (c) 3.5 - 3.005 = 0.495 kg = 495 g. Sneha put 5 in the tenths place both times, which is wrong.

questions.q: Find the sum: 4.6 + 2.8
questions.a: 7.4: 6 tenths + 8 tenths = 14 tenths = 1 unit and 4 tenths, so 4 + 2 + 1 = 7 units and 4 tenths.

questions.q: Find the difference: 9 - 3.45
questions.a: 5.55: write 9 as 9.00 and subtract column by column, borrowing across the point.

questions.q: Assertion (A): To add 12 and 3.75 in columns, 12 can be written as 12.00. Reason (R): 12 and 12.00 have the same value.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: because 12.00 has the same value as 12, writing it so lines up the places without changing the sum.

questions.q: Arjun goes to a stationery shop in Mangaluru with ₹500. He buys a geometry box for ₹137.50 and a pen set for ₹89.75. (a) How much does he spend? (b) How much money is left? (c) Can he also buy a dictionary that costs ₹275? Explain.

Ashwin cycles to train for a race. He rides 12.75 km on Day 1, 9.8 km on Day 2 and 14.065 km on Day 3. Over the four days from Day 1 to Day 4 he rides 50 km in all. (a) Find the distance for the first three days. (b) Find the distance on Day 4. (c) On which day did he ride the most, and on which day the least? (d) Find the difference between the longest and the shortest ride. (e) His target was at least 12.5 km every day. On which day did he miss it, and by how much?

Lakshmi buys groceries for a family function at a shop in Warangal: rice 5.5 kg, dal 2.75 kg, sugar 1.8 kg and cooking oil 0.975 kg. She will carry them home on a cycle-rickshaw whose owner agrees to carry at most 10 kg in one trip; anything more needs a second trip. (a) Find the total weight of the groceries. (b) By how much is the total above the 10 kg limit? (c) She will leave exactly one item for a second trip. Which item should she leave so that the first trip is as close to 10 kg as possible without going over? Show the weight of the first trip.
questions.a: (a) 5.5 + 2.75 + 1.8 + 0.975 = 11.025 kg. (b) 11.025 - 10 = 1.025 kg. (c) Leaving oil gives 10.05 kg (over the limit); leaving sugar gives 9.225 kg; leaving dal gives 8.275 kg; leaving rice gives 5.525 kg. She should leave the sugar: the first trip is 9.225 kg.
s: Part (c): tests the choices and decides to leave the sugar, first trip 9.225 kg

questions.q: Using the whole-number parts, the sum 14.6 + 7.9 must lie between
questions.a: 21 and 23: the sum is more than 14 + 7 = 21 and less than 21 + 2 = 23.

questions.q: A faulty adding machine shows one of these results for 38.45 + 26.7. Using only the whole-number parts, which result could be correct?
questions.a: 65.15: the sum must be more than 38 + 26 = 64 and less than 66, and only 65.15 lies in that range.

questions.q: True or False: Without adding, we can say that 5.3 + 2.4 is less than 9. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. The whole-number parts add to 5 + 2 = 7, and each decimal part is less than 1, so the sum is less than 7 + 2 = 9 (it is 7.7).
s: Uses the whole-number parts to bound the sum below 9

questions.q: (a) Using the whole-number parts, between which two whole numbers must 23.48 + 9.67 lie? (b) Find the exact sum and check that it lies in that range.
questions.a: (a) More than 23 + 9 = 32 and less than 32 + 2 = 34. (b) 23.48 + 9.67 = 33.15, which is between 32 and 34.

questions.q: Sonu's rule says the sum of two decimal numbers is greater than the sum of their whole-number parts and less than that sum plus 2. Ananya says the rule works for any two numbers, even 7 and 3. (a) What range does the rule give for 7 + 3? (b) Does 7 + 3 fit that range? (c) What must be true about the two numbers for the 'greater than' part of the rule to hold?
questions.a: (a) Greater than 7 + 3 = 10 and less than 12. (b) No: 7 + 3 = 10, which is not greater than 10. (c) At least one of the numbers must have a non-zero part after the decimal point; the rule is about decimal numbers, so Ananya's claim is wrong for whole numbers.
s: Part (b): 10 is not greater than 10, so it does not fit
Part (c): at least one number needs a non-zero decimal part

questions.q: Dinesh has ₹100 and wants to buy three things: a cap for ₹34.75, a bottle for ₹28.90 and a book for ₹36.20. (a) Using the whole-number parts, give a range for the total cost. (b) Can this estimate alone tell him whether ₹100 is enough? Explain. (c) Find the exact total. (d) Decide whether he can buy all three, and say how much money is left or needed.
questions.a: (a) Whole parts give 34 + 28 + 36 = 98; each of the three decimal parts is less than 1, so the total is more than 98 and less than 101. (b) No: 100 lies inside the range 98 to 101, so the estimate cannot decide. (c) 34.75 + 28.90 + 36.20 = ₹99.85. (d) Yes, he can buy all three; ₹0.15 (15 paise) is left.
s: Part (b): estimate cannot decide since 100 is inside the range
Part (d): can buy all three, ₹0.15 left

questions.q: In a cricket match the scoreboard shows 'Overs left: 3.2'. This means
questions.a: 3 overs and 2 balls are left, because the digit after the point counts balls out of 6, not tenths.

questions.q: A bus journey takes 1.5 hours. In hours and minutes this is
questions.a: 1 hour 30 minutes: each tenth of an hour is 6 minutes, so 0.5 hour is 30 minutes.

questions.q: Match each quantity in Column I with its meaning in Column II (1 hour = 60 minutes, 1 foot = 12 inches, 1 over = 6 balls). Column I: 1. 0.5 hour, 2. 0.3 hour, 3. 0.5 foot, 4. the '.5' in 'Overs left: 2.5'. Column II: A. 6 inches, B. 5 balls, C. 30 minutes, D. 18 minutes.
questions.a: 1-C, 2-D, 3-A, 4-B: 0.5 hour is 30 minutes, 0.3 hour is 3 x 6 = 18 minutes, 0.5 foot is 6 inches, and '.5' in overs means 5 balls.

questions.q: True or False: Asha's dance practice video on her tablet is 0.2 hour long, so it lasts 20 minutes. Give the reason or the correct length.
questions.a: False. 0.2 hour is 2 tenths of an hour, and each tenth of an hour is 60 / 10 = 6 minutes, so 0.2 hour = 12 minutes, not 20 minutes.
s: Shows a tenth of an hour is 6 minutes and gives 12 minutes

questions.q: A booking app says a train journey from Tirupati takes 2.7 hours. The train leaves at 9:25 a.m. (a) How many minutes is 0.7 hour? (b) At what time does the train arrive? (c) Rahul reads 2.7 hours as 2 hours 7 minutes. By how many minutes is his arrival time wrong?
questions.a: (a) Each tenth of an hour is 6 minutes, so 0.7 hour = 42 minutes. (b) 9:25 a.m. + 2 hours 42 minutes = 12:07 p.m. (c) Rahul gets 9:25 + 2 hours 7 minutes = 11:32 a.m., which is 35 minutes too early.

questions.q: In a 20-over inter-school final in Ranchi, an innings has 120 balls because 1 over has 6 balls. The chasing team needs 31 more runs to win when the scoreboard shows 'Overs left: 4.3'. In the last 3 complete overs the team scored 18 runs. (a) How many balls are left? (b) What does 'Overs bowled' show at this moment? (c) How many runs per ball did the team score in the last 3 overs? (d) If the team keeps scoring at this rate for every ball left, will it reach 31 runs? Show the runs it would make and by how many it would win or fall short.
questions.a: (a) 'Overs left: 4.3' means 4 overs and 3 balls = 4 x 6 + 3 = 27 balls. (b) 120 - 27 = 93 balls = 15 overs and 3 balls, shown as 15.3. (c) 3 overs = 18 balls, and 18 runs in 18 balls is 1 run per ball. (d) At 1 run per ball the team makes 27 runs in the 27 balls left. 27 is less than 31, so it falls short by 4 runs; it must score faster to win.
s: Part (c): 18 runs in 18 balls = 1 run per ball
Part (d): 27 runs, not enough, short by 4

questions.q: What is the next term of the sequence 2.3, 2.6, 2.9, ...?
questions.a: 3.2: the change is 0.3 each time, and 2.9 + 0.3 = 3.2.

questions.q: Which of these numbers is closest to 2: 1.91, 2.1, 2.08, 1.9?
questions.a: 2.08: it is 0.08 away from 2, while 1.91 is 0.09 away and 2.1 and 1.9 are each 0.1 away.

questions.q: Look at the sequence 7.5, 7.2, 6.9, ... which changes by the same amount each time. Statement I: The change is 'subtract 0.3'. Statement II: The 5th term is 6.3. Statement III: 6 is a term of this sequence. Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: All three statements are correct: the terms are 7.5, 7.2, 6.9, 6.6, 6.3, 6.0, so the 5th term is 6.3 and the 6th term is 6.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 3.1 is closer to 3 than 2.95 is. Reason (R): 3.1 is greater than 3.
o: A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
questions.a: A is false, but R is true: 3.1 is 0.1 away from 3 but 2.95 is only 0.05 away, so A is false; R is true, but being greater says nothing about closeness.

questions.q: (a) Find the change from each term to the next in the sequence 15.6, 15.25, 14.9, ... (b) Write the next two terms.

Meera is training for a district run in Warangal. Each day she runs a little more on the school track: Day 1 1.4 km, Day 2 1.75 km, Day 3 2.1 km, and the distance keeps growing by the same amount each day. (a) By how much does her distance grow each day? (b) How far will she run on Day 7? (c) Her coach wants her to run at least 4 km in a day. On which day does she first reach this? (d) On which day is her distance closest to 3 km?
questions.a: (a) 1.75 - 1.4 = 0.35 km each day. (b) Day 4 2.45, Day 5 2.8, Day 6 3.15, Day 7 3.5 km. (c) Day 8 3.85 km is still below 4 km and Day 9 4.2 km is above it, so Day 9. (d) Day 5 (2.8 km) is 0.2 km from 3 km and Day 6 (3.15 km) is 0.15 km from it, so Day 6.
s: Part (c): Day 9, since Day 8 is only 3.85 km
